Lake District Passes: Difficulty Rating

The Lake District's mountain passes range from gentle scenic routes to England's most challenging roads. Know what you're getting into before you go. Read our Lake District Mountain Passes by Motorcycle: Complete Guide guide for more. Read our UK Top 10 Mountain Passes for Motorcyclists guide for more.

  1. Hardknott Pass — 5/5. 33% gradient, tight hairpins, narrow single track. England's toughest.
  2. Wrynose Pass — 4/5. 25% gradient, connects to Hardknott for the ultimate combo.
  3. Honister Pass — 4/5. 25% gradient, quarry road with dramatic views.
  4. Kirkstone Pass — 3/5. 20% gradient, good surface, stunning Ullswater views.
  5. Newlands Pass — 2/5. Gentle climb, beautiful valley, quieter route.
  6. Whinlatter Pass — 2/5. Forest road, wide and well-surfaced.
Ride Hardknott and Wrynose early morning to avoid tourist traffic. Fuel up in Ambleside — no stations on the passes.
keyTakeaways: Hardknott Pass is the hardest at 5/5, with a 33% gradient and tight hairpins on narrow single-track.
Wrynose Pass at 4/5 connects to Hardknott for the ultimate Lake District combo.
Honister Pass scores 4/5 with a 25% gradient and dramatic quarry-road views.
Newlands and Whinlatter are the gentlest passes at 2/5 for building confidence.
Fuel up in Ambleside, as there are no petrol stations on the passes.

faq.q: Which Lake District pass is the hardest?
faq.a: Hardknott Pass is the toughest at 5/5. Its 33% gradient, tight hairpins and narrow single-track make it England's most challenging road. Combined with neighbouring Wrynose Pass at 4/5, it forms a demanding back-to-back challenge. Ride it early morning in the dry, and be ready to use passing places when you meet oncoming traffic.

faq.q: Which passes are best for less confident riders?
faq.a: Newlands and Whinlatter Passes, both rated 2/5, are the gentlest options. Newlands is a quiet, scenic valley climb, while Whinlatter is a wide, well-surfaced forest road. Kirkstone at 3/5 is a step up but has a good surface and stunning Ullswater views, making it a great progression before tackling the steeper passes.

faq.q: Can I ride Hardknott and Wrynose together?
faq.a: Yes, the two passes connect directly and are often ridden back-to-back for the ultimate Lake District combo. Together they deliver relentless gradients and hairpins, so take breaks and stay within your limits. Ride them early morning to avoid tourist traffic and coaches, which struggle on the steep, narrow sections.

faq.q: Where can I refuel near the Lake District passes?
faq.a: There are no petrol stations on the passes themselves, so fill up in Ambleside, Keswick or Windermere before you head into the fells. Fuel is sparse and often pricier in the central Lakes, so start with a full tank and plan your route around the towns on the periphery to avoid running dry.

faq.q: What conditions make the passes more dangerous?
faq.a: Wet weather dramatically raises the difficulty, as steep gradients and hairpins become slippery, especially on Hardknott and Honister. Fallen leaves in autumn, standing water, and loose gravel washed onto bends all reduce grip. Tourist traffic in summer and ice in winter add further risk, so pick your day and pace carefully.
